Continence is more excellent than marriage, 1, 42. Continence is commended, 1, 207; 2, 32; 4, 47. At what times married persons ought to abstain, 15, 163.

### Banquets

What sort of banquets bishops’ banquets ought to be, 15, 75. Presbyters and clerics are to avoid drunkenness and feasting, and how they ought to conduct themselves at banquets, 6, 252. Banquets according to pagan rites are to be abhorred, 11, 61.

### Bodies of Saints. See Relics. Corporals and Palls

They must be washed in a vessel assigned to that purpose alone, 1, 208. The corporal must be made of the cleanest linen, 2, 133, 134. It must not be made of silk or cloth [of another kind], and it is to be consecrated by a bishop, 2, 133, 134. A corporal must not be thrown into a fire in order to extinguish the fire, 15, 172.

### Body of Christ. See Eucharist. Likewise Incarnation. Human Body

Concerning the formed body [of an unborn child], 10, 58. Anyone may lawfully provide for the protection of his own body, 10, 118.

### Correction

For an excess in correction, forgiveness need not be sought from subjects, 6, 384. People must be rebuked, 10, 64. To rebuke one’s neighbor is to love him, 10, 52, 76. The purpose of correction, 17, 75. He who does not rebuke when he can is blameworthy, 10, 70. Sound reason ought to correct what a disturbed mind has sinned, 14, 19. A sin must not be imputed to one’s neighbor before he has first been reproved privately, 15, 129.

### Gluttony or Feasting. See Drunkenness. Creation

All creatures are corporeal, 17, 53. Why creatures are good, and why mutable, 1, 21, 22. Creator and creature are of the same nature, 1, 21, 22. Creatures endowed with reason are mutable, 1, 23.

### Creditor. See Debtor. Cross

The sign of the cross is applied everywhere, 1, 114. Feast of the Finding of the Holy Cross, 4, 5.

### Fault

The truth of an accusation must be diligently investigated before punishment, 9, 126. The guilt is greater if, through envy, an innocent person is handed over to the authorities to be killed than if those authorities themselves, through fear of some powerful person, were to kill someone, [Col. 1352] 10, 100. Those who defend deserters are blameworthy, 14, 110. Diversity of faults produces diversity of penances, 15, 47. Those who are guilty are by no means to be defended, 15, 121.

### Curiosity

Superstitious observation of times is to be avoided, 4, 1.

## D

### Demoniac. See Possessed Person. Demon. See Devil. Eternal Damnation and Hell

The saints do not pray for the damned, 17, 82. There is one fire of Gehenna, but it does not torment all in one and the same manner, 17, 80. The fire of hell does not shine, but tortures, 17, 90. It is corporeal, 17, 93. Incorporeal souls are tormented by the corporeal fire of hell, 17, 97, 100. The punishment of the damned is twofold, both of mind and of body, 17, 102.

### Damage

Concerning those who injure people, whether by obstructing roads, polluting springs, or contriving something similar, 16, 217, 219. Concerning compensation for damage caused by a slave, 16, 267. By what penalty damages inflicted are to be repaired, 16, 282, 349, 353. Accidental damage, 16, 172.

### Conjugal Debt. See Husband and Wife; likewise Marriage. Debt and Creditor. Likewise Debtor

Concerning debtors, 16, 28, 322. One who promises a debt is bound to payment, 16, 322. What a creditor ought to do when a debt is not paid on the appointed day, 16, 117. What a debtor who lacks the means to pay his debts ought to do, 16, 118. What a debtor who intends to frustrate his creditor ought to suffer, 16, 124. What ought to be done against one who harasses his sick debtor or impedes a deceased debtor’s funeral, 16, 134. How debtors’ evasions are to be judged, 16, 152. He who pays on another’s behalf releases that other person, 16, 167. An honorable thing given may be reclaimed, 16, 174. Claiming a debt by oath, 16, 196. Concerning debts to be paid, goods given on credit, and set-off, 16, 228, 229. Sureties must regard themselves as equally responsible for payment of the debt, 16, 255. No one may hold a debtor while disregarding the surety, 16, 359.

### Tithes

Tithes are to be paid to the Church, 3, 174, 196, 200. Laypeople must not receive tithes, 3, 281. The Church must not be defrauded of its tithes, 3, 284; 16, 338. Concerning the administration of tithes, 15, 149. Tithes are to be rendered even to newly established churches, 16, 263.

### Decrees and Statutes

The statutes of the Fathers are to be observed, 3, 142. When statutes should be moderated, 3, 141. If anyone acts contrary to a bishop’s decree, he is to be expelled from the church, 16, 15. Decrees together with bishops’ judgments are to be observed, 16, 312. The decretal letters of the supreme pontiffs are to be received with reverence, 4, 64.

### Deceased. See Dead. Degradation and Deposition

A cleric who is abusive or a malefactor is to be degraded, 11, 11, 28. A cleric who is a murderer or consults diviners is to be deposed, 10, 174; 11, 73. Flattering clerics, and those who stroll about at fairs or in the marketplace, are to be degraded, 6, 267. Concerning degraded presbyters, 6, 236. What is to be done even with those irrecoverably deposed, 6, 124. How those unjustly degraded are to be restored, 6, 237.

### Deposit

If anyone gives a deposit to another, he should employ three witnesses, 16, 136. One who, fearing prejudice, refuses to provide a surety may deposit some specified item of his property as a penalty, 16, 260.

### God

God is substance, 1, 2. What is to be thought concerning God, 1, 2. Likewise, 1, 4. The attributes of God, 1, 5, 17, 175. God’s knowledge is unchangeable, 1, 33, 34. Concerning God’s foreknowledge and providence, 17, 32, 38. What the right and left hand of God are, 17, 59. What God’s oath and repentance are, 12, 67. Concerning his eternity, 17, 33. Nothing happens without God’s counsel, 17, 34. Whatever God commands must be carried out, 4, 178. Why God is called jealous, angry, repentant, merciful, and foreknowing, 17, 87. His divinity cannot be seen, 2, 7, 10. Concerning those who wish to entrust their property to the cause of God, 16, 265. God created three living spirits, 17, 21.

### Devil or Demon

The nature of demons, 11, 70. Their divination, 11, 71, 72. The countless multitude of demons, variously assailing humankind, 11, 106. “Devil” is the name of an operation, not of a nature, 11, 50. The devil does not see inner thoughts, but sometimes understands them from bodily movement, 15, 119. Unclean spirits roam through the air, 17, 60. The devil is always ready to deceive: an example of this matter, 17, 64. The devil’s will is always wicked, but his power is never unjust, 17, 62. God speaks to the devil in four ways, and the devil to God in three ways, [Col. 1353] 17, 63. Concerning those who sacrifice to demons, 11, 39, 56; or invoke demons, 11, 55. Nothing from the threshing floor or winepress is to be sacrificed to demons, 11, 98. Concerning the unspeakable sexual intercourse of demons with women, 11, 105. Those who attempt to bind baptized persons to the sacrileges of demons are spiritually murderers, 11, 99.

### Deacon

The office of deacons, 1, 68, 252; 2, 79; 6, 10, 20, 306. A deacon is also called a Levite and may baptize, 6, 79, but not in the presence of a bishop and presbyter, 6, 99. Even a suspended deacon may baptize in necessity, 6, 368. When necessity compels, they may also administer the body of Christ to the faithful, 2, 23. They must not hand the sacred Eucharist to priests or sit among them, 2, 36. The age required for consecrating deacons, 5, 365; 6, 31. How they are to be ordained, 6, 13. The chastity and continence of deacons, 6, 68. The lawful wife of a deacon may not marry another, 6, 84. A deacon must not sit before a presbyter, 6, 123, 296, 375. The number of deacons to be appointed in churches, 6, 243. A deacon may not impose penance on anyone, 15, 134. In the absence of a presbyter, a deacon may, when necessity compels, receive a penitent, 15, 162. How a fallen deacon ought to be reconciled, 6, 67.

### Defamation, Detraction, or Abuse

How one who secretly defames another is to be corrected and punished, 6, 381, 404. No one, especially a priest, is to be defamed, 6, 430. Detractors are murderers, 10, 157. Malicious speech is a great crime, 13, 52. Murmurers, detractors, and contentious persons must be disciplined, 13, 53, 63, 64. A cleric who maligns a priest must ask forgiveness, 13, 66. Concerning the penance of detractors, 13, 67. Girls or women must not be disparaged, 15, 147.

### Dionysius the Areopagite (Saint)

Praise of Saint Dionysius the Areopagite, 4, 90. His writings are highly useful to the Church, 4, 90. A distinguished saying of his concerning the offering of the Mass, 3, 67. His book *On the Divine Names* was sent by Charles, king of the Franks, to Pope Nicholas, 4, 104.

### Dioscorus

Dioscorus, patriarch of Alexandria, was condemned at the Council of Chalcedon, principally because he had wrongfully excommunicated Saint Pope Leo, 5, 8. Though dead, he nevertheless remained excommunicated, 14, 62.

### Dissensions, Quarrels, Contentions, and Lawsuits

How contentions are to be ended, 3, 205; 4, 192. Disputes and dissensions must not be heard on fast days, 4, 46. People are to be exhorted toward peace rather than dissension and litigation, 5, 203. Bishops must restrain disagreements among clerics, 6, 290. Dissension and discord among brothers are a great evil, 5, 229, 231. Contentious and litigious persons are to be restrained, 13, 56, 58. Those in dissension who refuse to return to peace are to be excommunicated, 13, 59. The pleas of litigants must suffer no prejudice because of the ruler’s occupations, 16, 120. Concerning persons fighting, if one or the other has been struck, 16, 348.

### Divination. See Diviner. Divinity. See God. The Rich and Riches

Who among the rich are saved, 1, 311.

### Divorce or Dismissal of a Wife

If a husband is rough and unkempt, there ought not on that account to be divorce between husband and wife, 8, 232. A married man ought not easily to divorce, 8, 237. One who dismisses his wife without cause is to be punished, 8, 241. A wife must be dismissed if she compels one to abandon God, 6, 248. A wife is not to be cast aside because of barrenness, 8, 254. A woman must not depart from her own husband, 8, 317. Outsiders ought not, except from necessity, to create dissension among blood relatives, 8, 57.

### The Lord’s Day

No fasting on the Lord’s Day, 4, 7, 27, 51; nor kneeling, 4, 18. The solemnity of the Lord’s Day, 4, 13. On the Lord’s Day one must refrain from every illicit servile work, especially trade and business in the courts, 4, 16, 21, 53. What works may be done on Sundays, 4, 20. A bishop ought not judge cases on the Lord’s Day, 5, 204. Mass must be heard on the Lord’s Day, 6, 310. On Sunday abstinence must be kept from sexual pleasure, 8, 83. Nor are weddings to be celebrated then, 15, 165.

### Our Lord. See God or Christ. Donatists

Why reformed Donatists were permitted to minister, 6, 387.

## E

### Drunkenness, Feasting, and Gluttony

[Col. 1354]

Drunkenness is to be avoided, part 6, ch. 252; 13, 70, 84. How drunkenness is to be eliminated, 13, 68. Gluttony especially disgraces a Christian, 13, 69. Bishops and ministers of God must not devote themselves to feasting and drunkenness, 13, 71. Wine is to be shunned as poison, 13, 80. Concerning the penance to be performed by those who gorge themselves with wine, 13, 79, 81; or who make others drunk, 13, 83. Concerning the penance to be imposed on drunken ecclesiastics, 13, 76. Evils resulting from drunkenness, 13, 45.

### Church

The sacraments exist only in the Catholic Church, 1, 36, 37. Both good and bad are admitted into the Church, 1, 43. The unity of the Church, 5, 361. The more authoritative usage of the Church is to be maintained, 2, 79. The Church resembles a ship, 3, 1. What the Church is, 3, 3; and what ought to be done in it, 3, 71, 275. The Church’s authority, 14, 47. The mother Church, 3, 4, 27. Why churches are called basilicas, 3, 83. Individual churches ought to have prelates, 5, 356. Dogs are to be excluded from entry into churches, 3, 2. The construction of churches and monasteries, 3, 5. The manner, rite, and ceremony for building a basilica, 3, 8. Bishops have authority over the churches that lie within their dioceses, 3, 10. Concerning unconsecrated churches, 3, 11. Concerning the consecration of churches, 3, 13, 25, 326. The Church is to be honored, 3, 84, 150; 6, 283; 14, 93. Immunity of churches, and concerning those who flee to them, 3, 107; 6, 370; 10, 81; 16, 238. The Church must not be avaricious, 3, 180, 251. The Church possesses the spiritual sword, 8, 333. Exchange and transfer of churches, 3, 39, 80. How parish churches are to be ordered, 3, 47. Concerning the consecration of heretics’ churches, 3, 37. Nothing is to be taken away from the revenues of churches, 3, 12, 29, 56, 140, 148; 5, 6, 3, 156, 257; 14, 94. How, and into how many parts, church goods are to be divided, 3, 203, 161, 262. What is given to a bishop for the redemption of souls must be left to the Church, 5, 331. The endowment of a church pertains to the bishop’s ordination and authority, 3, 23, 209. The Church does not kill, 10, 7. No one may carry a sword in church except the king, 15, 174. Evil conversations must never be heard in the church courtyard or in the church itself, 15, 175. Laypersons’ buildings must not be erected in a church courtyard, 15, 178. No layperson may entrust his church to a presbyter except with the bishop’s permission, 15, 179. The Church’s privileges must in no way be violated, 16, 238, 298. How great and what kinds of dangers the Church suffers, 16, 1. Holy Church has one Father in heaven, 16, 33. Whatever is obtained by those who seek the Church’s property from kings ought to be void, 16, 37. One who does not communicate with the Church must not perform public duties, 16, 158.

### Ecclesiastics. See Ecclesiastical Ministers; likewise Cleric. Roman Church

The Roman Church is holy, undefiled, and apostolic, 1, 87; 5, 42. The laws and decrees of the Roman Church are to be revered and observed, 1, 135; 4, 211, 238; 5, 31. The faith of the Holy Roman Church, 2, 10; 3, 4. The custom of the Church is to be followed in practice, 3, 47; 4, 39. The Roman Church’s custom concerning sponsors, 1, 218; and concerning deacons and subdeacons, 2, 79. What the Roman Church rejects must be rejected, 4, 75, 79. Violators of the statutes of the Roman pontiffs are to be excommunicated, 4, 205; 5, 35. The authority and primacy of the Holy Roman Church, 4, 101; 5, 2, 6, 9, 17, 21, 26, 40. Vicars of the Roman see do not possess the fullness of apostolic power, 5, 11. Doubtful and more difficult cases are to be referred to the Apostolic See, 5, 30, 294.

### Almsgiving

How alms are to be bestowed, 17, 129. Almsgiving is of no value when one’s life is not corrected, 17, 121, 126. Whether almsgiving should be performed during a fast, 4, 44. Prayer with almsgiving is very good, 6, 166. Alms are not to be accepted from an excommunicated person, 14, 68. Almsgiving extinguishes sins; nevertheless, one must not therefore sin in order to give alms, but should give alms because one has sinned, 15, 70; 17, 130. Almsgiving expiates many evils, 15, 126. Surplus goods are to be distributed to the poor, 15, 128.

### Buying and Selling

Concerning things for sale, 16, 244. Buyers and sellers are scarcely free from fault, 13, 25. It is fraud to store up grain in expensive times so that it may be sold at a higher price, 13, 26. A thing is not alienated when it is sold for less than it has been entrusted at, 16, 178. One who knowingly buys a stolen thing must restore it, 16, 215. Concerning one who sells another’s property for less, 16, 232. No one may sell any property without the owner’s consent, 16, 221. Nothing is to be bought from an unknown person, 16, 308. Concerning one who sells property of others bought through malicious contrivance, 16, 342.

### Possessed Person or Demoniac

Possessed persons are to be baptized, 1, 247. Sacred mysteries must not be entrusted to those afflicted by a demon, [Col. 1355] 2, 88; 6, 40. Possessed persons ought to sweep the church, 3, 21. How persons afflicted by the devil are to be freed, 6, 256. Exorcists must provide food for possessed persons, 3, 263. Possessed persons must not be initiated into holy orders, 6, 135. How demoniacs may be cured, 11, 102. Communion is not forbidden to demoniacs, 11, 103. Demoniacal clerics cannot ascend to higher orders, 11, 104; 15, 105.

### Epiphany or Theophany

The feast of Epiphany is venerable, 1, 47; 4, 9. On the Lord’s Epiphany, three readings from Isaiah are read, 4, 63.

### Bishops or Prelates of the Church

Bishops ought to visit their churches and dioceses, 1, 75; 3, 38, 132, 136; 5, 180, 341. What they ought to investigate while visiting, 1, 75; 5, 19. During their visitations they must summon the people, 5, 196. If they cannot visit personally, they may perform this through others of reputable life, 5, 193. Bishops are not to be appointed in villages and small towns, 5, 142. Concerning vicious bishops, 1, 150. The office and obligation of a good shepherd, 5, 318, 324, 372; 6, 20. Bishops are to be obeyed, 5, 225, 233, 360, 238; 14, 121. Bishops may not be transferred, 1, 152. After one bishop has been consecrated, there cannot be a second, 5, 359. Bishops are bound to confer confirmation while fasting, 1, 261. They must preach, 5, 198, 209, 370; and protect the poor, 16, 2, 4. They must avoid shameful profit and ostentation, 1, 287, 271; 2, 115; 3, 42, 132, 141. In necessity a bishop may assist his household from the Church’s treasury, 2, 141. Concerning a bishop in another’s diocese, 1, 301; 5, 210. When episcopal sees may be transferred, 3, 79; 5, 125. A bishop who has used secular authority to obtain a church is to be deposed, 3, 85; likewise if he has alienated church property, 3, 172. A church must neither be entrusted to nor taken away from a presbyter without the bishop’s consent, 3, 88. How bishops ought to administer church resources, 3, 147, 160, 167, 202, 211; 16, 5. They must not sell them, 3, 141; make testamentary dispositions concerning them, 5, 326; or give or alienate them, 5, 127. On an altar at which a bishop has celebrated Mass, no presbyter may celebrate that day, 3, 170.

Bishops must not teach grammar, 4, 161; 5, 199, nor read pagan books, 4, 160, 165. A bishop’s minister or vicar must not be a layman, 5, 194, 195. What sort of person he must be, 6, 194, 195. The loftiness, excellence, and power of the episcopal order, 5, 178; 14, 1. How bishops ought to exercise it, 14, 3. While a bishop lives, no one may be ordained [in his place], 5, 302, 304, 336, 352, unless the bishop has long and seriously been ill, 5, 302, 307. How an accused bishop ought to clear himself, 5, 301, 342; 6, 272. Rebuke of a prelate who keeps a concubine, 5, 310. Rebuke of an elderly bishop, 5, 312. Bishops must not bear arms, 5, 332. They must not excommunicate for a personal injury, 5, 351. They are not to be ordained unwillingly, 5, 347. A person ordained by a bishop who has been condemned must not be defended, 6, 230. An accused bishop must not be abandoned by his own people before the conclusion of his case, 6, 340. Why a bishop ought to be the husband of one wife, 8, 294. When a bishop has been killed, another must not be substituted until the offenders have been identified and punished, 10, 19. It does not become a bishop to pronounce a hasty judgment, 14, 18. Prelates are thrones of God, 16, 296, and must in no way be troubled, 16, 296. The beginning of the episcopal order, 5, 1. Its purpose, 5, 226, 372. A higher prelate must not be judged by an inferior, 5, 8. When a bishop ought to use the pallium, 5, 20. He must receive it from the Apostolic See within three months, 5, 136. Bishops occupy the place of the apostles, presbyters that of the seventy-two disciples, 5, 58, 98. Who are to be promoted to the episcopate, 5, 59, 90. Bishops-elect must first be examined, 5, 62, 105. The ordinations of bishops must be performed, by apostolic authority, by all the bishops of the province, 5, 65, 69. A bishop must be endowed with learning and virtue, 5, 68, 372. A bishop is not to be ordained against the will of clergy or people, or without the metropolitan’s knowledge, 5, 61, 65. How those who object to a prelate’s election are to be examined, 5, 60. When a bishop is to be excommunicated, 5, 297; 14, 16. Proud and negligent prelates should be called dogs rather than princes, 5, 67, 317. A layman must be thirty years old to be chosen bishop, 5, 70. One must ascend to the episcopate through the ecclesiastical grades, 5, 72, 102. Whoever obtains a bishopric through ambition is to be deprived of lay communion, 5, 73, and condemned most severely, 5, 133. Simony must be entirely excluded from the episcopate, 5, 75, 122. The simoniacally ordained and the ordainer are to be excommunicated, 7, 78, 127. A prelate must vow that he will defend the Catholic faith, etc., 5, 84. An archbishop’s judgment is void without the assent of his fellow bishops, 5, 96, 101; the same is to be held concerning a bishop’s judgment when clerics are absent, 5, 214. A bishop who seeks a higher see must both lose his own and fail to obtain the other, 5, 103; 6, 73.

[Col. 1356] How a pontiff is to be elected, ordained, and consecrated, 5, 124, 138, 139, 140, 338; 6, 113. At what age, 6, 29. A bishop must not be made through payment or the patronage of persons, 5, 129. In electing a bishop, the common good must be sought, 5, 130. A bishop’s ordination must not be long delayed, 5, 135, 137. A bishop consecrated by only two bishops is to be rejected, 5, 141; likewise one who stirs up sedition, neglects to go to the church committed to him, or invades a church not his own is to be rejected and deprived of communion, 5, 147. Bishops ought especially to reside in their own dioceses, 5, 148, 176, 217, 340, 350. Order among bishops is to be maintained, 5, 164, 337. A bishop must be forbidden to invade another diocese or move from his own to another, 5, 150, 173, 177, 179, 184, 236. Because of persecution, a bishop may migrate to another church, 5, 186, 219, 223. He must not neglect his cathedral church, 5, 187. He must have with him priests and clerics of proven life, 5, 205. He ought to live as though a guest, 5, 205. How a visiting bishop is to be received, 5, 216, 221. Bishops are to be judged by the Lord, 5, 232. Accusations against a bishop are not lightly to be admitted, 5, 234, 237, 243, 250, 264, 271, 299. How and where accused bishops are to be judged, 5, 245, 258, 260, 270, 280, 335. They must not be condemned without the authority of the Roman pontiff, 5, 292. Which accuser of a bishop is to be admitted and which is not, 5, 289.

### Eucharist

The Eucharist is administered to the newly baptized, 1, 160. It benefits those who receive it unworthily in no respect, 1, 185. How the Eucharist becomes the sacrament of Christ’s body and blood, 2, 1, 4, and of what it consists, 2, 9, 68. The bread which the Lord Jesus broke and the cup which he gave to his disciples are his body and blood, 2, 5. How one ought to approach Holy Communion, 2, 6, 24, 25, 32. Christ’s body in the Eucharist is neither divided nor diminished, 2, 7. The properties and effects of this sacrament, 2, 7. The distinction among communicants, 2, 8. The reality of Christ’s body in the sacrament, 2, 9, 10. The Lord’s body is to be kept in a pyx, 2, 19, and must always be present in the church, 2, 20. Daily communion, 2, 25; 1, 28. At what time communion is to be received, 2, 25; 1, 28. Likewise, 2, 27, 29. Those who do not approach Holy Communion at Christmas, Easter, and Pentecost are not to be counted among Catholics, 2, 33. Communion received by criminals benefits them nothing, 1, 185. Persons must come fasting to communion, 2, 45. Stale Eucharistic species are to be burned, 2, 45. The sacred host dipped in blood must by no means be offered to the people, 2, 85. Fragments of hosts are not to be consumed by laypeople, 2, 86. Concerning the distribution or requiring of Holy Communion, 2, 92. The Eucharist must not be placed in lay hands, 2, 129. The form of words to be used in administering the Holy Eucharist, 2, 129. Communion must not be denied to persons who are to be fastened to gibbets, 14, 124. The viaticum of Christ’s body is to be administered to those at the point of death, 15, 31, 33. A certain apostate was healed from a grave illness through the power of the divine viaticum, 15, 37.

### Eunuch

A eunuch must not be ordained, 6, 37. When a eunuch, or castrated man, may be ordained, 6, 75, 374.

### Eusebius of Caesarea

His *Chronicle*, or *History*, is not to be rejected, 4, 82. The *Apocrypha* of the history of Eusebius Pamphilus, 4, 65.

### Gospel

To evangelize is preferable to baptizing, 1, 70. Truth is in the Gospel, 2, 6. One must stand while the Gospel is read, 2, 138; 6, 93.

### Excommunication and Anathema, or Curse

The deserved punishment of a certain excommunicated person, 5, 378. What it is to anathematize, 14, 49. How grave is the danger of being anathematized, 14, 50, 52. Excommunicated persons will be deprived of eternal life, 2, 101; 14, 53. The distinction between excommunication and anathema, 14, 51. Why excommunication is pronounced, 3, 122, 126. Excommunicated persons must pursue their case within a year, 14, 111. One must not communicate with an excommunicated person, 14, 95, 97. Those who are to be excommunicated, 3, 140, 150, 155, 156, 208; 14, 83, 122. Concerning those who die excommunicated, 14, 114. Consecration must not be performed by excommunicated persons, 5, 134. An excommunicated person condemns himself by communicating, 5, 314. Excommunicated persons must receive communion where they were excluded, 14, 105. No one is to be excommunicated except for a grave cause and before the ground of excommunication has been proven, 5, 371; 21, 41, 42, 80, 81. What is to be done concerning persons ordained by excommunicated persons, 6, 406. An excommunicated person is to be punished, 5, 314, 362; 14, 79. The saints do not sin when they excommunicate sinners or strike them with a sentence of curse, 14, 4. Those who bind a just person or absolve an unjust one are abominable to God, 14, 6. A curse is pronounced in two ways, 14, 5. When an excommunicated person is to be reconciled, 14, 15. One who communicates with excommunicated persons is excommunicated, [Col. 1357] 14, 23. The Church’s sacraments are not to be received from excommunicated persons, 14, 36. A person excommunicated by his own bishop must by no means be received by others, 14, 37, 206. Whether an entire household is to be struck with anathema when one person commits a sin, 14, 44. An example of excommunication, 14, 45, 46. An excommunicated person cannot excommunicate, 14, 57. One must not communicate with the dead with whom one did not communicate in life, 14, 60. The names of excommunicated persons must be recorded, 14, 65, and affixed to the doors of the church, 14, 113. An excommunicated person’s gift is not to be accepted unless he repents, 14, 67. An excommunicated person cannot accuse, 14, 69. No one can excommunicate unless he has the authority, 14, 71. Formula of excommunication, 14, 75.

### Disinheriting

The Church may not be made heir when a son has been disinherited, 3, 177. Ecclesiastics must not accept property from those whose children or relatives would on that account be disinherited, 16, 261.

### Exorcist

The office of exorcists, 3, 263; 6, 7, 20, 298. How an exorcist is to be ordained, 6, 16.

### Extreme Unction. See Sick Person.

## F

### Servant. See Freedman. Woman

A woman must not enter the sanctuary, approach the altar, or handle Christ’s body, 2, 39, 72, 135. A woman who has given birth may receive communion, 2, 62. Women should take care to prepare linens for altars, 3, 91. They are forbidden to touch sacred vessels, 3, 265. Which women may live with clerics and presbyters, 6, 52, 81, 189. Familiarity with women is to be avoided, 6, 77, 89. A woman ought not to wear male clothing, 7, 78; 11, 64; nor teach, perform any office of ecclesiastical order, 7, 101, 102, or plead cases anywhere, 7, 103. Why women veil their heads, 8, 92. Their heads ought not to be shorn, 8, 320. A woman who suffocates a fetus not yet born, or kills it after birth, is to be punished most severely, 9, 102; 10, 181, 186. One must not approach a menstruating woman, 9, 119. A woman undergoing penance must not marry another after her husband’s death, 15, 72. A woman must not enter a church before the cleansing of her blood, 15, 151. What woman is infamous, 16, 125.

### Usurer and Usury

It especially disgraces an ecclesiastic to be a usurer, 13, 8. Otherwise he is to be deposed and even excommunicated, 13, 17, 14. Who is a usurer, 13, 17. What usury is, 13, 22.

### Feast and Festival

The feast of a church’s dedication is to be celebrated with an octave, 3, 24; 4, 14. Feast of the Finding of the Holy Cross, 4, 5. The feasts of Easter, the Nativity, Epiphany, and the Ascension of the Lord, likewise Pentecost and the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist, are to be celebrated jointly, 4, 9. The feasts of Saint Stephen, John the Evangelist, the Innocents, Silvester, the Circumcision, the Purification, the Assumption and Nativity of the Blessed Mary, the twelve apostles, Michael, Lawrence, All Saints, and Saint Martin are to be kept as holidays, 4, 14. Concerning the observance of feasts, 6, 36. Saints’ feasts are not to be celebrated during Lent, 4, 43. Feasts must be announced to the people by presbyters, 4, 14, 15. The festivals of heretics are hateful to God, 2, 108.

### Faith

Faith must be held and preserved with utmost constancy, 1, 44. The necessity of faith for salvation is supreme, 6, 158. If faith is given for committing a sin, whether it should be called faith, 12, 14. Good faith is contrary to fraud, 16, 176.

### Children. Likewise Father and Mother

Children are bound to obey their parents, 6, 163. Money must not be entrusted to sons under paternal authority without their father’s knowledge, 16, 230. The dishonor of parents does not harm children who live honorably, 16, 413. Concerning the condemnation of priests’ sons, 6, 425. Children are legitimate if born of a woman with whom a man had cohabited before contracting marriage, 8, 34. An illegitimate son born of a nobleman and a slave woman, 8, 67. Who are the children called *quaesiti* (“sought”), 8, 69. Illegitimate children follow their mother rather than their father, 8, 70. Children must not despise their parents on the pretext of religion, 8, 319. One who abandons his own children is to be excommunicated, 8, 318. The property of an incestuous father is due to his children, even those born from another wife, 9, 4. Concerning the penance to be imposed on children who do not preserve honor toward their parents, 15, 106. No one may claim abandoned children, of whatever condition, as his own property, 16, 97. A woman who marries a second time cannot recover property given by her to her children, 16, 126. Concerning those who are born differently, 16, 193. How natural children are made legitimate, 16, 141.

### Scourges of God

[Col. 1358]

How pestilence, famine, irregularity of the weather, and other injuries of the air, together with the remaining scourges of God, are to be repelled, 4, 50; 6, 166: by fasts and prayer, 4, 50; 6, 166.

### Fornication or Sexual Impurity

A wife may be dismissed on account of fornication, 8, 43, 228. Fornication is prohibited, 8, 72. An unmarried man fornicating with an unmarried woman must do penance for three years, 8, 205. Infidelity is fornication, 8, 247. What fornication is, 8, 275. Sexual impurity and fornication are grave sins, 8, 276, 278. Every illicit sexual union is understood under the name *moechia* (“adultery”), 8, 279. Fornication is greater after the Gospel than before, 8, 310. Concerning women who have committed fornication and kill their offspring, 8, 314, 331. A woman with whom both father and son have fornicated must never be joined in marriage, 9, 76. Concerning women and nuns who fornicate with one another, 9, 83. Concerning irrational intercourse, sodomy, bestiality, and sin against nature, 9, 88, 105, 128. Penance is to be imposed on those who perpetrate such unspeakable crimes, 9, 107. Concerning the penance to be imposed on clerics or monks who indecently pursue little boys, 9, 93. The dreadful torment of a certain fornicator, 9, 98. The prayers of saints do not benefit those assailed by the spirit of fornication unless they themselves also pray, fast, groan, etc., for themselves, 9, 99. Corruptors of boys are to be barred from communion, 9, 109. Natural intercourse with one’s own wife is venial; with another’s wife it is condemnable, 9, 110. A disordered movement occurring without the consent of the bodily members is without fault, 9, 123. What it is to misuse one’s wife; there is no fellowship in dishonorable acts, 11, 14; 16, 176. Those whose speech is lascivious are to be given a penance of three days, 13, 57. Concerning clerics who sin by a bodily offense, or fall through sudden weakness of the flesh, 14, 86, 87.

### Franks or Gauls

Praise of the Franks, 2, 96. The goodwill and favor of the supreme pontiffs toward the kings of the Gauls, 5, 378, 358. Pope Leo writes to the army of the Franks that they will attain the kingdoms of heaven if they are killed in defense of Christians, 10, 87. Pope Adrian anathematizes Tassilo, duke of Bavaria, unless he obey Charles the Great and the Frankish people, 10, 89. In Gaul and certain other provinces, no one establishes churches except those whom Saint Peter the Apostle or his successors have appointed as priests, 4, 67.

### Thief or Robber, and Theft
Theft is not committed without an intention to steal, 16, 105. Theft is theft in a small matter just as in a great one, 13, 41. On the penance of a thief, 13, 42. Stolen goods are not to be received by the Church together with any avaricious motive. How thieves are to be convicted, 13, 5. And punished, 16, 207. Prayers are not to be offered for thieves killed in the act of theft, 13, 45. Robbers are to be excommunicated, 14, 82, 109. On the penance to be imposed on those who, after capturing a robber, subsequently killed him, 13, 46, 47. He does good who disables a robber or pirate, 10, 113. Those who arrange for Christians to be plundered: to what penance they ought to be subject, 15, 115. What has been acquired by theft ought not to be converted into a partnership, 16, 176. One who kills a thief in the act of stealing is not guilty of homicide, 16, 211, 352. If anyone unknowingly buys something from a thief, he ought to seek out the seller, 16, 212. Knowing receivers and accomplices of thieves are to be regarded as thieves, 16, 216. Robbers are not to be received as guests, 16, 223. One who apprehends a robber ought to suffer no loss, 16, 236. An invader is to lose what he seized, 16, 243. To what a person who has confessed theft is bound, 16, 294. If anyone invites others to plunder, what is to be done to him, 16, 311.

### Madman and madness

Madmen are not to be punished, 13, 86, 91. Madness does not permit marriage to be contracted, but does not impede one validly contracted, 13, 87. A madman is incapable of conducting affairs, 13, 89. He cannot make a will, 13, 93. Whatever an angry mind does, it considers just, 16, 30.

## G

### Gaul. See Franks. Gelasius (St.)

He wrote many highly useful books, 4, 94. His decrees concerning authentic books, etc., 4, 64.

### Gentiles. See Pagans. Genuflections

God is to be prayed to and worshipped with genuflections, 3, 276. Genuflections are not made on more solemn days, 3, 276. One does not kneel on Sundays or during Pentecost, 4, 18. When “Let us bend the knee” is to be said in the Mass, 4, 36.

### Germanus (St)

St Germanus, bishop of Paris, excommunicated King Charibert, 5, 378.

### Gerontocomium

A venerable place in which poor persons and persons infirm solely because of old age reside, 17, 137 [Col. 1359]. The immovable property of this institution may be alienated according to the Leonine constitution, 17, 137.

### Degrees of kinship or consanguinity; likewise affinity or spiritual relationship

Marriage cannot take place in the fourth degree, 9, 5, 20. How degrees of consanguinity are to be counted, 9, 6, 13, 15, 177. Consanguinity ends with six branches, 9, 7. Neither by alms nor by fasts, nor by any means, may anyone retain with himself his female blood-relative, 9, 9. A wife is not to be taken from one’s own kindred, 9, 11, 15, 39, 42. No one is to be joined to blood-relatives [the Latin reading is corrupt], 9, 12, 30. The measure of guilt is to be treated according to the degrees of kinship, 9, 14. What is meant by: “Children born of relatives shall die,” 9, 18. He who takes his brother’s wife by reason of kinship is to be anathematized, 9, 19. Two brothers may take two wives, 9, 27. Which persons may not be taken in marriage because of kinship, 9, 21. Those who take female blood-relatives as wives are infamous and accursed, 9, 22. Intercourse with a stepmother is a great crime, 9, 28. Marriage ought not to be dissolved because of consanguinity, 9, 32. There is a spiritual relationship between a godfather and godchild, 9, 34. No one is to marry either his godchild or his godmother, 9, 36. After his wife’s death no one may marry his godmother, 8, 35. Concerning one who took the blood-relative of his concubine, though she had been betrothed to another, 9, 37. In what line marriages may be made, 9, 46, 54. The faithful ought not to be joined in marriage as far as the seventh generation, 9, 26. A man is not related in the same manner to his own blood-relatives and to those of his wife, 9, 43. The kinship of husband and wife is to be considered in one manner, 9, 44. By how many witnesses consanguinity is to be proved, 9, 52. What is to be done if no one is willing to confirm consanguinity by oath, 9, 53. Within seven degrees are contained all names of relationships, 9, 64. A woman who married two brothers is to be excommunicated, 9, 67. Concerning one who defiled two sisters, 9, 69. He who marries his stepdaughter, etc., 9, 71. Whether anyone may marry the wife of his deceased godfather, 9, 96. Whether anyone may marry the daughter of his godmother, 9, 97. Who are agnates and cognates, 46, 326.

### Grace

Without the aid of divine grace we are able to perform no good work, 1, 32. Divine grace both forgives sins and supplies help so that they are not committed again, 17, 30.

### Gregory, pope (St)

On his forty homilies and *Synodical Booklet*, 4, 96. On his letters, 4, 144.

### Gluttony. See Abstinence.

## H

### Heir

We ought to make God our heir, 3, 207. If heirs do not fulfil the testator’s commands, the bishop ought to fulfil them, 16, 35. Within a year the heir is to pay the legacies, 16, 116. Which actions pass to heirs, 16, 202. After her husband’s death, a wife ought to possess her dowry, and this does not belong to the heirs of the deceased, 16, 246. An heir may not act contrary to a prior just decision, 16, 300. Concerning one who, lacking children, wishes to have another as his heir in their place, 16, 302.

### Heresy and heretic

Why heretics are destined for eternal fire, 1, 38, 39. Who are heretics, 16, 158. One must not communicate with deceivers of the people, that is, with heretics, 2, 95; 15, 117. How one should associate with deceiving priests, etc., 2, 96, 113. God rejects the festivals of heretics, 2, 108. The baptism of heretics, 1, 233. The blessings of heretics are curses, 3, 260. *Eulogiae*—blessed bread or gifts—are by no means to be accepted from them, 3, 269. Ecclesiastics are not to be permitted to approach heretical cemeteries, 3, 259. By whom the books of heretics may be read, 4, 84. Heretics are devotees of dialectic, 4, 229. Marriages are not to be contracted with heretics, 8, 204. Judges persecuting heretics and despoiling their goods are not to be blamed, 10, 75. Heretics ought not to administer public offices, 16, 158. Even after death they are to be anathematized, 14, 62. On heretics returning to the unity of the Catholic Church, 1, 283; 6, 390, 97. Why those returning from heresy are permitted to exercise their offices, etc., 6, 385, 387. Formula for renouncing heresy, 5, 344.

### Soothsayer and haruspex, or diviner, etc.

Those who observe soothsayers and such persons are excommunicated, 11, 1; 35, 37. What the Pythian spirit is, 11, 6. Days, Kalends, and omens are by no means to be observed, 11, 7, 16, 19, 43. Diviners are not to be believed, 11, 10. Sorcerers are to be condemned, 11, 8. The courses of the stars or the flight of birds are not to be observed, 11, 9, 40. Nor are Egyptian days to be observed, 11, 15. Astrologers (*planetarii*; in French, I think, “makers of almanacs”), mathematicians, soothsayers, etc., are to be condemned, 11, 20, 24. No faith is to be placed in lots, 11, 21, 52. Who are diviners by lots, 11, 22. On correcting one who accused a woman by magical art, 11, 25 [Col. 1360]. Diviners by lots and sorcerers are to be driven out, 11, 30, 49. Trees are not to be worshipped; but if there are any to which the populace attributes honour, they are to be burned, 10, 31, 38. Vain observances concerning herbs and springs are to be avoided, 11, 47, 48, 57. Nothing is to be drunk or eaten in order to overturn God’s judgment, 11, 51. Inventors of magic and necromancy, 11, 67. Various kinds of divination, 11, 68. Their causes, etc., 11, 69. On certain execrable remedies, 11, 69. Enchanters and others of this kind contribute nothing to human health; rather, they are like snares by which the devil deceives many, 11, 65. On the nature of the penance to be imposed on those who make outcries and practise sorcery when the moon is eclipsed, 11, 58. Those who use incantations, 11, 74.

### Henry, emperor

His constitutional agreement with the Roman pontiff, 5, 52.

### Henry, king

Leo IX, pope, writes to Henry, king of the Franks, son and heir of King Robert, concerning Bertha his wife, 9, 8.

### Herod

He ought not to have kept his unjust oath, 12, 53, 73.

### Jerome, priest (St)

His writings are received by the Church, 4, 64. The *Lives of the Fathers*, which he compiled, are to be received with every honour, 4, 64. But other *Lives of the Fathers*, written without trustworthy authors, are never to be read, 4, 141. He composed the book *On Ecclesiastical Writers*, 4, 89.

### Hilary of Poitiers (St)

St Hilary, bishop of Poitiers and doctor of the Church, is commended, together with his writings, 4, 237. His works are numbered among the authentic writings, 4, 64, 87, 92, 99.

### History

On the authority of ecclesiastical history, 4, 143.

### Actor

Actors ruin boys, 11, 83. Whether they ought to be admitted to Holy Communion, 1, 31. Ecclesiastics ought to avoid them, 5, 339. A certain actor playing a cymbal suddenly dies, 10, 67. It is an enormous vice to give one’s goods to actors, 11, 84. Nothing is to be given to actors or hunters, 13, 31.

### Homicide and murderers

Three kinds of murderers, 10, 157. How one who kills his wife ought to do penance, 8, 126. All laws prohibit homicide, 10, 1. One who kills himself is a murderer, 10, 4. Such a person must moreover be deprived of offerings and Masses, 10, 5. Compensation for priests slain must be paid to the bishop, 10, 9; 10, 140. On compensation for an ecclesiastical person killed, 10, 9. On the penance of one who has laid violent hands upon an ecclesiastic, 10, 10, 12, 16. How a priest accused of being the murderer of his prelate ought to clear himself, 10, 15. Assailants and murderers, especially of ecclesiastics, are to be punished and excommunicated, 10, 17, 20, 38, 137, 158. On the correction, condemnation, and penance of those who grievously strike, mutilate, or kill others, 10, 21, 33, 39, 42, 50, 153, 155; 15, 113, 131. On seven years’ penance for homicides not committed voluntarily, 10, 25, 28, 144. One who kills, without cause, either his own or another’s slave ought to be punished equally, 16, 186.

Those who kill sleeping persons are murderers, 10, 27. On one who kills by order of a ruler, 16, 289. Poisoners are to be punished capitally, 11, 26. On the penance of one who laid hands on a bishop, 13, 65. Those who were not present at a homicide but merely arrived while it was being committed are not to be punished, 10, 30. On the differing penalties to be imposed upon those who wound or shed blood, 16, 204. A woman is culpable if her mules trample a person to death, 10, 32. An intention to kill is treated as the deed itself, 10, 46; 15, 132. A person ought not to be killed except by command of law, 10, 41; 16, 80. A reprieve is to be granted to a person before he is put to death, 10, 47. On various homicides and their penalties, 10, 49. A bishop who is a murderer is to be excommunicated and deposed, 10, 52. Those are not to be deemed murderers who kill either thieves breaking into a house or excommunicated persons through zeal for the Church, 10, 53, 54. On those who kill embryos in the womb, 10, 53. An unformed conception does not count as homicide, 10, 56. Not everyone who kills is a murderer, 10, 65; 16, 78, 172. He is not cruel who slays the cruel, 10, 112. One who kills in obedience to authority is not guilty of homicide, 10, 98, 101, 104. An officer of a judge who kills of his own accord is a murderer, 10, 103. On voluntary homicides and the manner of their penance, 10, 130, 141, 146. On murders and accusations involving bishops and the remaining orders of the Church, 10, 124, 135. On homicide and accidental injury, 10, 150, 172. Those who give counsel to kill become murderers, 10, 160. On several persons attacking one person who afterwards died, 10, 170. One who sells a Christian is a murderer, 10, 176. No Mass is to be celebrated for those who inflict death upon themselves, or who are punished for their crimes; nor are their bodies to be buried with chant, 10, 108; 15, 140 [Col. 1361]. Human beings are ministers and avengers of God’s wrath, 10, 111. They may lawfully provide for the protection of their own bodies, 10, 118. Persons of every condition can please God, 11, 82. This alone is human righteousness: that one rebuke oneself, 15, 67. Every human being is a sinner, 15, 137, 138. The dignity of the human condition, 17, 1. A human being consists of two substances, 17, 17. Spirit is not a third substance in the human being, 17, 18. The miseries of human beings, 17, 26.

### Hospitality

It is to be practised by clerics and priests, 6, 257. Those who neglect hospitality ought to fulfil the penance imposed upon them, 15, 127.

### Sacred victim. See Eucharist. Humility

The practice of humility is especially fitting for prelates, 5, 322. One must not lie for the sake of humility, 12, 42.

### Hymns: *Gloria in excelsis Deo*, *Te Deum laudamus*

The hymn *Gloria in excelsis* is to be sung at Mass on Thursday in the Lord’s Supper; *Te Deum laudamus* is sung in thanksgiving, 10, 135.

### Hypocrite

One must not communicate with hypocrites and deceivers of the people, 2, 95.

## I

### Ignorance

The mother of all errors, 5, 202.

### Nocturnal pollution

Whether, after a nocturnal pollution has occurred, one may celebrate or communicate, 2, 52. On the cause of pollutions, 9, 111.

### Image

Veneration of sacred images, 3, 41. That synod in which holy images were condemned was rejected, 4, 142. The image of the Lamb, precursor of the Lord, 4, 122. Images of our Lord Jesus Christ are ordered to be painted, 4, 122. The image of Christ the Saviour sent to the city of Edessa, 4, 83.

### Immersion

On triple immersion in baptism, 1, 126, 128, 194. What that triple immersion signifies, 1, 126, 128, 194.

### Immovable and movable property

Immovable property attached to a church may be exchanged for the goods of another church, 3, 189. The immovable property of certain sacred places may be alienated, 17, 137.

### Unchastity. See Fornication. Incantation. See Soothsayer. Incarnation

What is to be held concerning the Incarnation of the divine Word, 1, 3, 16, 20. The Son alone was incarnate, 1, 13. The Son, or divine Word, was conceived, 1, 13. Likewise, 1, 18. He has true flesh, 1, 20; and a true soul, 1, 14. By his Incarnation Christ recovered lost goods, 17, 19.

### Arsonist

The penance of arsonists, 3, 127. Burnings and plunderings of ecclesiastical property must be repaired, 13, 36. Arsonists and mutilators are to be excluded from communion, 13, 40. An arsonist must restore everything burned, 15, 146. Arsonists are to be punished by the most severe penalties, 16, 329.

### Incense

Incense is used in the offering of the body and blood of the Lord, 3, 267.

### Incest

On secret incest, 15, 53. The violation of a veiled virgin is incest, 7, 124. By what punishment an incestuous marriage is to be punished, 16, 122. The incest of nuns is graver than adultery, 7, 130. Between which persons incest occurs, 9, 1. The penalty of an incestuous person, 9, 3. Who are incestuous, 9, 25. Their infamy is indelible, 9, 23; 16, 313. After worthy penance, they may contract marriage, 8, 31. An incestuous person is to be excommunicated, 9, 40; and restrained, 9, 65, 125. On various forms of incest, 9, 77. What is to be done concerning an incestuous person who moves from one bishopric to another, 9, 101.

### Defame. See Slander. Infants and minors

Infants and little children are to be baptized, 1, 226, 228. Unknown infants are to be exposed before the doors of a church, 3, 252, 253. Before baptism, infants are bound by the sins of their parents, 17, 8. On miscarriages and unformed births, 17, 9. A *brephotrophium* is a place in which infants are reared, 17, 137. Its immovable property may lawfully be alienated in necessity, 17, 137. Minors are incapable of making a will, 13, 93.

### Hell. See Damnation. Unbelievers and idolaters. See Pagans. Sick persons. On the baptism of sick persons. See Baptism.

Sick persons are to receive communion from a priest, 2, 39; and to be anointed with holy oil, 2, 75; 15, 27 [Col. 1362]. Sick persons are to be nourished, 15, 125. On those who, through fear of death, confess their sins in their illness itself, 15, 28. Illness prevents abstinence and fasting, 15, 168. The immovable property of a hospital, or place in which the sick are treated, may be alienated, 17, 137. Sick persons ought to confess their sins, 15, 36. They may drink and eat at every hour, 15, 42.

### Enemy

Intimate enemies are to be cast off, 6, 339. Enemies who refuse reconciliation are to be excommunicated, 13, 59. How one ought to behave toward an enemy, 14, 22. One who forgives his enemy fulfils these words of the Lord’s Prayer: “Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors,” 17, 125. One who is disposed to ask forgiveness is not to be regarded as an enemy, 17, 127. Prayer is to be offered for enemies, 17, 131.

### Injury

Injury is to be repelled, 10, 120. Force and injury are to be resisted, 10, 191. One compelled to suffer losses for a moderate injury becomes infamous, 16, 330.

### Innocent, pope

He excommunicated Emperor Arcadius, 5, 378.

### Insanity and foolishness

An insane murderer, 10, 154. On a penitent who has fallen into insanity or frenzy, 15, 8.

### Insane person. See Madman. Documents

Documents ought not to be made without the subscription of witnesses, 16, 137. A notary who drew up alienations of Church property is to be banished into perpetual exile, 17, 137.

### Interdict

Why an interdict is pronounced, 3, 122.

### Investiture

Nothing is to be given for the investiture of any church or benefice, 3, 90.

### Isidore

His chapters on the seven degrees of consanguinity; likewise, the tree of consanguinity, 9, 64.

### Ishmael

Why Abraham cast him out, 8, 61.

### Israelites

Why they did not commit theft in despoiling the Egyptians, 13, 2. In the last days they will be converted through the preaching of the Church, 17, 108.

## J

### Fasting

Fasting is to be undertaken with the consent of superiors, part 4, chapter 59. A proclaimed fast is to be observed, 15, 181. On a certain Alcibiades, who fasted indiscreetly, 4, 58. One does not fast on Sunday, 4, 7. Appointed fasts are to be observed, 4, 14, 31, 33. The fast of the Four Seasons is not to be omitted, 4, 26, 35; 6, 74. A fast is not to be broken on Friday, 4, 33. On the Wednesday fast, 4, 32. Contemners of fasting are to be anathematized, 4, 73. Fasting is to be joined to almsgiving, that is, to good works, 4, 44. A fast is not to take place without some refreshment, 4, 55. The usefulness of fasting, 4, 57. Indiscreet fasts are by no means to be accepted, 4, 58. It profits nothing to fast from foods and to err through sins, 13, 34.

### Rogation fast. See Rogations. Jest. See Play. Judas the traitor

He received the Eucharist just as the other apostles did, 2, 105. One who steals anything from a church is likened to Judas the traitor, 14, 89.

### Jews

Outside the Catholic Church they are not saved, 1, 38, 99. Public offices are not to be entrusted to Jews, 13, 97, 118. Their testimony is to be weakened, 13, 96. They are not to be compelled by force to baptism and the Christian faith, 1, 179, 276, 285; 13, 94, 110. They are to be led to the Christian faith by gentleness, 13, 101. They are to be examined before baptism, 1, 275. After a fast of forty days, Jews are to be baptized on Sunday, 1, 61. Their children are to be baptized and separated from their parents, 1, 277. On Jews who have apostatized from Christianity, 1, 279. Christians ought not to be subordinated to or serve Jews, 1, 282, 183; 13, 103, 110. Christian slaves of Jews are to be granted freedom, 1, 280; 13, 106; 16, 32. Jews ought not to buy Christian slaves, 13, 98. Who is a Jew, 2, 7. On the penance to be imposed upon one who kills a Jew, 10, 162. One must not participate with them in their errors, 13, 95. Christians ought not to attend Jewish banquets, 13, 99, 117. From the Lord’s Supper until the following Monday, Jews ought not to appear in public, 13, 100. They ought to retain their ancient synagogues, 13, 104. Their slaves fleeing to a church are to be protected, 13, 102, 11. They ought not to be excluded from their religious observances, 13, 205. They are not to be harassed, 13, 107, 104. They have lost the power to wage war, 13, 108. They are to be condemned to perpetual exile and proscribed if they circumcise a Christian, 13, 109. Careful inquiry is to be made concerning Jewish slaves, 13, 113 [Col. 1363]. Medicine is not to be received from a Jew, 13, 116. On the penance of those who have eaten with a Jew, 13, 119. Converted Jews are to be honoured, 13, 112.

### Judge

The derivation of the word *judge* (*judex*), 10, 116. A judge is not to be despised, 16, 133. His authority, 10, 2. Who is fit to judge and adjudicate, 10, 60. No one may kill except a judge, 10, 78. Officers of judges are not condemned on account of their administration, 10, 94. When a judge exacts punishment, he does not return evil for evil, 10, 102; 4, 114. A judge may exact punishment, 10, 106. A judge is not the author of crime but the minister of law, 10, 15. No one ought to judge another before God judges the matter, 16, 68. No one is to be sent to judgment without consent, 16, 345. A judge is not to be insulted, 16, 257. The cases of monks and nuns are to be heard not before a civil judge but before a bishop, 16, 146. Judges ought not to be hasty in carrying out a ruler’s orders, 16, 252. They ought to pronounce their judgment in writing, 16, 147. On those prevented from coming to judgment, 16, 163; or who, though lawfully summoned, refuse to come, 16, 258. No one is to be judge or arbiter in his own case, 16, 170. On one who is not judged justly, 1, 307. An unjust judge is to be committed to prison, 16, 318; and punished, 16, 339, 341. Judgment is not to be demanded concerning a case already adjudicated, 16, 333.

### Final judgment

On the final judgment, 1, 28. On the day of judgment the righteous will enjoy the glory of souls and bodies, 17, 77. When judgment is finished, there will be a new heaven and a new earth, and the conflagration of the world, 17, 119, 120. The impious will be condemned for their crimes, 17, 105. Before the day of judgment, the elect will be endangered at the coming of Antichrist, 17, 105. How the article of the Creed is to be understood: “He shall come to judge the living and the dead,” 17, 112. On the day of judgment sinners will be struck down, 17, 115. Then the elect and the reprobate will also be separated, 17, 116.

### To swear, oath, and promise

When one ought to swear, 3, 135. One must not swear by a creature, 6, 266, but by the Creator, 12, 6, 72. A certain form of oath, 9, 61; 12, 38. Oaths are not to be frequent, even under necessity, 12, 7. An oath is not contrary to the Lord’s commandment, 12, 3. One must not swear except in great necessity; conditions of an oath, 12, 76. One oath suffices to resolve the controversy of parties, 16, 132. One must not commit perjury, 12, 4; 24, 59. Oaths contrary to nature are not to be maintained, 12, 9; 15, 84. The force and necessity of an oath, 12, 2, 5. An unjust, harmful, and shameful agreement does not bind, 16, 165, 190. Unjust and harmful oaths are not to be kept, 12, 77, 53, 64, 75, 80. God receives an oath as the person to whom it is sworn understands it, 12, 36. The difference between a false and a true oath, 12, 39. Those who compel others to swear commit a grave offence, 9, 67. One must swear while fasting, 12, 69. Promises are not always to be fulfilled, 12, 17. On punishment and penance for perjury, 12, 18, 25, 27, 60, 66, 68, 71. What perjury is, 12, 22, 34; it is compared with adultery, 12, 21. Those who consented to perjury are infamous, 12, 26, 79. Concerning what matters an oath may be made, 12, 31; 58, 62. She who compels perjury is a murderess, 12, 28, 30. To whom a perjurer is to be denounced, 12, 29.

### Law and justice, or judgment

On divine and human law, 3, 194. Uncertain judgments are to be avoided, and how they are to be credited, 5, 244; 6, 329. Unjust judgments have no force, 6, 343. When judgment is to be made, 6, 317, 349, 430. An absent person is not to be judged, 6, 319. A judge should not fear to be judged in turn, 8, 392. The case of priests is not to be entrusted to another court, 6, 325. A reprieve is to be granted to one coming to judgment, 6, 335. The difference between an ecclesiastical and a secular case, 6, 336. The decision of chosen judges is not to be despised, 6, 365. A judgment unjustly approved is not to be feared at all, 14, 8. On rash judgment, 14, 10. Foreign judgments, 5, 260.

## L

### Manual labour

It is useful, 6, 177, 179. It is commended to clerics and priests, 6, 177, 179.

### Laity and secular persons

They ought to exercise no authority over ecclesiastics, 3, 87, 102, 138; 6, 408; nor dispose of their property, 7, 89; 16, 36. Laymen ought not to receive tithes, 3, 281. They are not to be elevated to ecclesiastical prelacies; or at least they are not to be promoted rashly or before their thirtieth year, 5, 59, 70, 71. They may not choose priests for themselves, 5, 63. They ought not to extort confession from priests, 5, 241. How a layman is to be promoted to holy orders, 6, 92, 95. Laymen must by no means presume to teach in the presence of clerics, 8, 323; 16, 13. Their testimony is not to be received in accusations against clerics, 6, 277, 313, 220. Bishops are by no means to be accused before secular authorities, 5, 277. Laymen ought not unjustly to bring accusations against a church or cleric, 16, 6 [Col. 1364]. They ought not to be present when ecclesiastical affairs are handled, 16, 12. The people are to be taught, not followed, 16, 14. Any layperson who harms his own people or homeland in adversity is to be excommunicated, 16, 25. Laypersons may compel priests serving their churches to do nothing other than celebrate the divine office, 16, 31. Anathema upon every secular person who inflicts injury on any cleric, 16, 206. Those who despise priests are to be restrained by secular power, 16, 345.

### The fallen

On the fallen and their penance, 6, 48. Those fallen into a sin of the flesh after receiving holy orders ought not to approach the altar, 6, 78. How the fallen are to be restored, 6, 85, 397. Whether those fallen while in holy orders can be restored, 15, 57. The sacred viaticum is to be administered to fallen persons at the point of death, 15, 33. What is to be done with the property of fallen priests and clerics, 6, 380.

### The good thief

The baptism and martyrdom of the good thief hanging on the cross, 1, 192. His repentance of a single moment obtained paradise, 15, 43.

### Lectians or Celestians

They were heretics; their error concerning baptism, 1, 53.

### Reading. See Book. Reader

A reader may be appointed by an abbot or chorepiscopus, 5, 376. The office of reader, 6, 6. How a reader is ordained, 6, 17. A cleric who has once performed the office of reader in any church is by no means to be retained by another, 7, 34. A layman ought not to recite a reading in church, 7, 105.

### Legate or messenger

The authority of a legate, 5, 28. The authority of an apostolic legate, 5, 27.

### Laws, customs, canons, or ecclesiastical constitutions

The old law is shadow; the Gospel is truth, 2, 6. Laws and customs not contrary to the Catholic faith are to be observed, 4, 66. Ecclesiastical statutes are to be observed, 4, 67, 69; 5, 171. Ecclesiastical customs are to be regarded as laws, 4, 68, 199. Ecclesiastical laws cannot be dissolved by the laws of rulers, 4, 187; 16, 38. Contemners of canons or ecclesiastical laws are to be anathematized, 4, 219; 16, 7, 8. The enactments of the Fathers are to be preserved, 4, 226. Canons ought to be learned by clerics and priests, 6, 250. God’s law does not compel one to do evil, 8, 259.

### Laws of rulers; local usage and customs

Imperial laws are not to be used in every ecclesiastical controversy, 4, 86. Long-standing customs resemble law, 16, 184. A law that pardons the past forbids for the future, 16, 192. Things instituted for permanent benefit ought to remain unshaken, 16, 317. Good laws and customs are not easily to be changed, 4, 204, 210; bad ones, however, are to be uprooted, 4, 203, 213; 16, 240. Customs become laws, 4, 194, yet do not prevail over laws, 4, 202. Custom yields to manifest truth, 4, 234. Kings are bound by their own laws, 16, 43. The laws of rulers ought to be subject to God’s law, 4, 86, 190. What an honourable law is, 4, 168. Laws ought to accord with reason, 4, 191. Temporal laws are to be observed, 4, 169, 186; 16, 242. Violators and contemners of laws are to be punished, 4, 181, 183. Whatever an emperor establishes by letter is law, 4, 173, 184. The laws of Christian rulers are to be accepted, 4, 176, 177. Ecclesiastics may invoke secular laws for their defence, 4, 183. Authority is not to be contradicted, 4, 322. Disputes and cases are to be settled according to the laws, 4, 192; 16, 149. Different laws do not dissolve a marriage that has been contracted, 8, 213. Usage ought to yield to authority, 4, 207.

### Pimps

Pimps are to be expelled from cities, 8, 305; 16, 121. One who possesses slaves for prostitution practises pimping, 8, 304. One who practises pimping is to be deprived of communion, 8, 306.

### Leo, pope

How he cleared himself of the crimes alleged against him, 5, 115, 342. St Leo’s letter to Flavian is numbered among authentic writings, 4, 64.

### Children. See Children. Freed persons and slaves, etc.

On freed persons and slaves manumitted by the Church, 3, 237, 244; 16, 50, 67. On a slave who has fled his master, 13, 48; 16, 55, 74, 75, 102, 186. Slaves are not to be ordained, 6, 41, 64, 100. Manumitted slaves may be ordained, 6, 108. Afterwards they must still honour their masters, 6, 302. A slave must not become a monk without his master’s knowledge, 7, 44, 48, 154; 16, 46; nor abandon his master, 14, 126. A freeborn woman who marries a slave becomes a handmaid, and a marriage between a slave and handmaid is not dissolved, 8, 52; 16, 335. A handmaid’s marriage with her master is lawful, 8, 150. Marriages contracted between a male slave and female slave with the master’s consent are not dissolved, 8, 157 [Col. 1365]. A marriage between a free man and a free woman is not dissolved if the free man subsequently becomes a slave, 8, 212. How a free person may distribute his goods as he wishes, 16, 277. How a free person may clear himself of theft, 16, 239. On those born of freeborn parents or parents of differing condition, 16, 185. Manumitted slaves are not to be enslaved again, 16, 48, 56, 73. The Church ought, if necessary, to protect freed persons, 16, 51. Whether the testimony of slaves is to be received, 16, 57, 103, 224. The punishment of a slave who informs against his master, 16, 356, 332. Ungrateful freed persons accusing their patrons are to be punished, 16, 62, 63, 93, 144. A slave fleeing to a church against his master’s will is not to be protected, 16, 68. No one may seize for his own use the slave of a cleric, 16, 70. A freed person ought not to accuse the Church of which he was a slave, 16, 65. One who conceals a fugitive slave is to be punished, 16, 71. Masters ought not to show themselves intolerable toward their slaves, 16, 76, 77. The duty of servants, 16, 82. A master ought to appease a slave whom he has unjustly injured, 16, 85. If a slave kills with the master’s knowledge, both remain culpable, 16, 79. It is not the slave but the master who is to be sued for recovery, 16, 86, 89. A master may reclaim without payment a slave unjustly abducted, 16, 87. On slaves who, without their master’s knowledge, inflict harm upon subjects, 16, 88, 94, 106. If a slave takes out a loan, whatever of it passes into the master’s use is to be paid by the master, 16, 90. On the offspring of a female slave, without the master’s knowledge, 16, 95; or on one born in this manner, 16, 189. The property of a condemned slave belongs to the master, 16, 98. The duty and authority of masters over slaves, 16, 99, 104, 210. If anyone buys from another’s slave without the master’s knowledge, then, if the master so chooses, the purchase has no validity, 16, 101. The slaves of others are not to be corrupted or solicited, 16, 108.

### Free will. See Will. Books and their reading

Which books are to be read in church, 3, 251. On reading to be conducted in church, 3, 250. Those who read prohibited books are excommunicated, 3, 251. Sacred Scripture is to be read in church, 3, 262; 4, 63. Which books are authentic, 4, 64, 72. Apocryphal books, 4, 65. To whom reading the books of heretics may be permitted, 4, 84. Secular books are not to be rejected altogether, 4, 85. The book of the *Lives of the Fathers*, 4, 141. Apocryphal books are not to be read, or at least are to be examined with great caution, 4, 153. Those who falsify the books of Catholics are to be excommunicated, 5, 158. Defamatory pamphlets are by no means to be written, 4, 156. On defamatory pamphlets and the punishment of their authors, 16, 235; 7, 248, 249. What the book of life is, 17, 117. Pagan books are not to be read, 16, 160. Books containing the fictions of poets are forbidden to be read, 4, 167. Bishops may read the books of heretics when necessity and occasion require, 4, 160. The usefulness of divine reading, 6, 177. On reading to be held at the divine table, 6, 260; and likewise on avoiding scurrilous matters, 6, 261, 402; 13, 75.

### Lawsuit. See Dissension. Litanies. See Rogations. Letters dimissory, etc.

A cleric cannot be ordained in another diocese without letters from his own bishop, 6, 144. Priests and deacons ought not to travel without letters from their bishop, 6, 145, 210, 213. An ordained priest ought to receive letters from his ordainer, 6, 147. Letters of recommendation are suitable for more honourable persons, 6, 216. It is fitting to aid poor exiles by letters of peace, 6, 216. On the use of *formatae* letters, 6, 217. On the manner of composing them, 6, 4, 33. An example of a *formata* letter, 6, 434, 435.

### Lot

Lot is excused for wishing to prostitute his daughters, 9, 114. He is called holy, 9, 115. He is to be blamed for drunkenness; in disorientation rather than by dispensation, he was handing over his daughters to be prostituted, 9, 117.

### Lothair

Having dismissed his lawful wife, he took another, 8, 225. He is rebuked, and the prelates consenting to this are deposed, 8, 226, 227. He committed adultery, 8, 261. Examination of his case, 8, 334. Waldrada, his illegitimate wife, 8, 334.

### Washing

The feet of those recently baptized are washed, 1, 195. The feet of guests are to be washed, 15, 127; 1, 195. The ceremony is called the *mandatum*, 15, 127; 1, 195. The washing or laundering of corporals and altar-cloths, 1, 208. Penance is to be imposed on one who has bathed with women, 15, 148.

### Profit

Just as profit, so loss is shared among partners, 16, 200. What shameful gain is, 13, 24.

### Louis

Louis, king of the Franks and emperor of the Romans, entered into a constitutional pact with the Roman pontiff, 5, 51. His royal generosity or liberality toward the Roman Church, 5, 51.

### Play or jest

[Col. 1366]

Indecent jokes are by no means to be made before prelates, 7, 110. Ecclesiastics ought not to delight in games, 11, 76. On feast days, one is not to occupy oneself with vain games, 11, 77. Jokes are to be avoided, 11, 80.

## M

### Curse. See Slander. Also Excommunication. Manna

Manna was a figure of the Holy Eucharist, 2, 2. Those who ate manna died, 2, 7, 2.

### Marcellinus, pope
S. Marcellinus, pope.

The lapse of St. Marcellinus, pope and martyr, and his subsequent glorious confession, 5, 8. He is not condemned by inferior bishops, 5, 8.

Marcellus, pope.

He established titular churches at Rome, on account of baptism and penance, 1, 57.

Mary the Virgin.

What kind of Virgin Mary was, 1, 196. Mary’s virginity and humility, 4, 224. The book called *The Passing of Mary* is apocryphal, 4, 65, 152.

Martyrdom.

On martyrdom, 1, 30, 211. The martyrs of the Church are to be venerated, 3, 263. Relics of martyrs are to be deposited in altars, 270. With what caution the Acts of the holy martyrs are to be read, 4, 64. Many martyrs rose again with their bodies, 4, 130. Those who swear falsely at the memorial shrines of martyrs are often seized by a demon, 12, 58. If anyone breaks idols and is killed there, he is by no means to be reckoned a martyr, 10, 172.

Marriage or matrimony.

On lawful marriages, 8, 40. What marriage is, 8, 1. Consent makes marriage, 8, 17; 16, 142. At what times it may be contracted, 15, 169. The inviolable sacrament of marriage, 8, 9, 12, 131. Marriage ought not to take place without a dowry, 8, 144. Every marriage is a union of spouses, 8, 277. Marriages are not dissolved on account of religion, 8, 129. Between separated spouses the bond of marriage remains, 6, 131; 8, 335. Continence is better than marriage, 1, 42. Clandestine marriages are forbidden, 8, 141. No one may contract marriage with a spiritual co-mother, 1, 135, 139; nor with his father’s stepdaughter, 1, 307. A marriage is not dissolved if a woman, unknowingly, marries a man who has taken a vow, 7, 10. A man who marries a veiled woman is to be excommunicated, 7, 131. A virgin or widow is not to be compelled into marriage, 8, 19. Marriage between relatives is forbidden, 8, 36. How error invalidates marriage, 8, 56, 164. When marriage becomes void, 8, 57; 16, 128. The end and use of marriage, 8, 82, 88. What sort of wife ought to be given in marriage, 8, 140. One who contracts an unlawful marriage becomes infamous, 16, 166. No one ought to marry a woman whom he has previously defiled through adultery, 8, 201, 211, 261. If one spouse becomes insane, the marriage is not dissolved, 1, 166. The marriages of slaves are lawful, 8, 167. The insane are incapable of contracting marriage, 8, 167. One man may not marry a girl who has been betrothed to another, 8, 169. On spouses unable to consummate marriage, 8, 178. What ought to be done if intercourse of this kind is prevented by sorcerers, 194. So long as her husband is absent, a wife absolutely may not contract marriage with another, 8, 189. If wives of men taken captive marry others, they must be reunited with their husbands when those husbands return from captivity, 1, 190, 193; 8, 244. Otherwise they are to be excommunicated, 8, 192. On a pagan who dismisses his pagan wife, 8, 195. On the baptized man whose wife is unbelieving, 8, 196. Crimes, not marriages, are dissolved by baptism, 8, 197. A spouse dismissed by another spouse must not marry someone else, 8, 200, 221, 230, 236, 239. Married persons who have separated ought to remain unmarried, 8, 208.

Maximianus.

Why Maximianus, bishop of Vaga, sought assistance from the emperor, 10, 59.

Lying.

What a lie is, 12, 48. Eight kinds of lies, 12, 1. Every lie must be avoided, 12, 41, 42, 49, 83. Even a joking lie must be avoided, 12, 43; and likewise an artful lie, 44. On the difference between lying and concealing a word, 17, 46. In some cases, being mistaken is not a sin, 45. Figurative speech is not a lie, 12, 47. What distinction there is between being deceived and lying, and between the will to deceive and the will to be deceived, 51. A certain lie is useful, 12, 53.

Prostitute.

What a prostitute and an outcast woman are, 8, 297. Prostitutes may choose an honorable life, 8, 37. They may be deemed eligible for marriage, 38. Foolish and unjust are those who keep prostitutes, 8, 233. One who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her, 8, 308, 313. What is given to a prostitute cannot be recovered, 8, 307. A bishop consenting to prostitutes was rebuked, 309. Prostitutes are forbidden, 8, 311.

Metropolitan bishop and metropolitan church.

The customs of metropolitan churches are to be observed by their suffragans, [Col. 1367] 3, 68. Clergy may complain to the metropolitan about their bishop, 3, 137. A metropolitan must seek the pallium from the supreme pontiff, 5, 354. Church property must by no means be alienated without consulting the metropolitan, 3, 153. What sort of letters he ought to send, 5, 158. He must hear a fellow-provincial bishop in his own case, 8, 169. A metropolitan ought to preserve his own rights, 5, 146. He must not presumptuously use the pallium, 5, 324; nor excommunicate another’s parishioner, 5, 100; 14, 72. His judgment is invalid without the assent of his fellow bishops, 5, 99, 101, 174. A province is by no means to be divided between two metropolitans, 5, 146.

Michael (St.).

He is prince of the angels. He was also once the angel of the synagogue of the Jews, 17, 61.

Soldier.

He ought to serve God and the Church, 10, 123. He ought not to be admitted into a monastery except after a three-year probation, 124. Military service is not a sin, 10, 125, 126. Soldiers are not to be received into the clergy, but only into the monastic habit, 127. If they wish to convert, they ought not to be hindered, 10, 128, 129. Neither pagans nor heretics ought to serve as soldiers, 11, 92.

Ecclesiastical ministers.

How they are to be honored, 6, 299. Their office, 6, 20. They are to be ordained in their own dioceses, 5, 178; 6, 42. If they do not freely discharge their office, they are to be deposed and punished, 1, 217, 240, 250. They ought to abhor shameful gain, 1, 71, 65, 271, 287. At times they may bear arms in self-defense, 10, 68; 10, 71, 73, 82. They ought not to be assailants, 5, 315; 6, 235, 291; 3. They ought to undertake nothing without permission from their own bishop, 2, 123; 3, 239; 4, 90; 6, 171. Privileges and immunity of ecclesiastics, 3, 56, 100, 151, 154, 175, 181; 5, 308. The goods of the Church, ecclesiastics, and pious institutions are by no means to be alienated, 3, 183, 192, 243; 17, 137. On bishops, presbyters, and deacons baptized again, 1, 293. Ordained ministers may communicate and approach the altar, 2, 42. What ecclesiastics ought to avoid, 5, 339, 353, 366, 370, 377; 6, 288. They are to be admitted into churches according to the bishop’s direction, 3, 190. For seven weeks before Easter they must abstain from meat and other luxuries, 4, 25. What books they ought not to read, 4, 162. How they are to be examined and judged when accused, 6, 280. How injuries inflicted upon clergy and monks are to be settled, 8, 401. Those inflicting them are to be anathematized, 6, 403. Particular offices are to be assigned to individual ecclesiastics in individual churches, 6, 344.

Human miseries. See *Man*. Mercy.

It is not to be forbidden, 6, 49. Works of mercy are to be performed for an afflicted neighbor, 15, 59.

Mass.

How it is to be celebrated, 2, 15, 63, 117; 3, 267. Preparation to be made before Mass, 3, 279. It is not to be celebrated by an illiterate or disreputable minister, 2, 44, 90. What is to be done if any of the Lord’s blood drips onto the ground, 2, 56, 61. Bishops and priests celebrating Mass must have prepared ministers with them, 2, 67. The number of Masses, 2, 81, 87. Prefaces of the Mass, 2, 77; 3, 69. The Lord’s body is to be received with the chalice, 2, 89, 114. The most sacred mysteries are by no means to be entrusted to persons troubled by a demon or illness, 2, 88. Mass is not to be celebrated in an unconsecrated place except in grave necessity, 2, 76; 3, 60, 59. Mass is to be celebrated at night only on the Nativity of the Lord, 2, 71. The hour for celebrating Mass, 2, 71; likewise, 2, 119; 3, 65. Mass is to be heard on the Lord’s Day, 2, 121; 6, 310. The people must attend the public Mass, that is, the parish Mass, 2, 119. Private Masses, 2, 119; 15, 176. A Mass is to be completed by another if the priest himself cannot complete it, 2, 124; 3, 271. Mass is to be celebrated with a minister, 2, 127; 3, 70. A trental of Masses for the dead, 17, 167. For which dead persons Masses are beneficial, and conversely, 17, 69. Presbyters ought to communicate after celebrating Mass, 2, 129. The people ought not to depart until Mass has been completed and the blessing given, 3, 34, 265. Clergy ought to hear Mass daily, 6, 243. Incense is used in the celebration of Mass, 3, 267. At the end the Gospel beginning “In the beginning” is said, 15, 176. It is forbidden to go to celebrate Mass carrying a staff or with the head veiled, 3, 172. Bishops ought frequently to celebrate Mass, 5, 207. When a priest celebrates Mass, all those standing around must respond to him, 8, 169; 7, 67. When Mass may be celebrated twice in one day, 3, 268. A presbyter may celebrate three Masses in one day, and no more, 15, 171. A presbyter who has drunk after cockcrow ought not, on the following day, unless necessity presses, to celebrate the solemn rites of Mass, 15, 170. Masses for the dead, 17, 66, 68. Examples on this subject.

Monk.

Monks ought to remain at rest and not wander through various places, 6, 214; 7, 8, 11, 150. Which monks are not to be promoted to the clergy, [Col. 1368] 7, 7. How those who abandon the monastic profession are to be punished, 7, 19, 28. How those wishing to become monks are to be tested, 7, 153. Clerics may become monks with the bishop’s permission, 6, 370. Baptisteries are to be excluded from monastic churches, 1, 55; nor are public Masses to be performed in them, 7, 13. Laymen ought not to preach to monks, 6, 249.
